label: Antioch
verse_text: As they served the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, “Separate Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work to which I have called them.”
note: The church at Antioch sends Barnabas and Saul.

label: Seleucia
verse_text: So, being sent out by the Holy Spirit, they went down to Seleucia. From there they sailed to Cyprus.
note: Antioch’s port at the mouth of the Orontes.

label: Salamis
verse_text: When they were at Salamis, they proclaimed God’s word in the Jewish synagogues. They also had John as their attendant.
note: They preach in the synagogues of Cyprus’s east coast.

label: Paphos
verse_text: But Saul, who is also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, fastened his eyes on him
note: The proconsul Sergius Paulus believes. Here Acts first calls Saul “Paul”.

label: Perga
verse_text: Now Paul and his company set sail from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia. John departed from them and returned to Jerusalem.
note: John Mark leaves them and goes back to Jerusalem.

label: Antioch in Pisidia
verse_text: But they, passing on from Perga, came to Antioch of Pisidia. They went into the synagogue on the Sabbath day and sat down.
note: Over the Taurus mountains to the plateau. Paul’s first recorded sermon.
letter_text: but you know that because of weakness in the flesh I preached the Good News to you the first time.
letter_why: If “Galatians” means these southern towns, as many read it, this is the first visit Paul remembers.

label: Iconium
verse_text: In Iconium, they entered together into the synagogue of the Jews, and so spoke that a great multitude both of Jews and of Greeks believed.
note: Many believe; the city divides, and they flee.

label: Lystra
verse_text: But some Jews from Antioch and Iconium came there, and having persuaded the multitudes, they stoned Paul and dragged him out of the city, supposing that he was dead.
note: A lame man walks; the crowd calls them gods, then stones Paul.
letter_text: persecutions, and sufferings—those things that happened to me at Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. I endured those persecutions. The Lord delivered me out of them all.
letter_why: Paul names Antioch, Iconium and Lystra among his sufferings.

label: Derbe
verse_text: When they had preached the Good News to that city and had made many disciples, they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,
note: The farthest town. Its site is not certain; this pin is the mound most often named.

label: Lystra
verse_text: When they had preached the Good News to that city and had made many disciples, they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,
note: Back the way they came, strengthening the new disciples.

label: Iconium
verse_text: When they had preached the Good News to that city and had made many disciples, they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,

label: Antioch in Pisidia
verse_text: When they had appointed elders for them in every assembly, and had prayed with fasting, they commended them to the Lord on whom they had believed.
note: They appoint elders in every church.

label: Perga
verse_text: When they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.

label: Attalia
verse_text: When they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.

label: Antioch
verse_text: When they had arrived and had gathered the assembly together, they reported all the things that God had done with them, and that he had opened a door of faith to the nations.
note: They tell the church how God “opened a door of faith to the nations”.

label: Antioch
verse_text: but Paul chose Silas and went out, being commended by the brothers to the grace of God.
note: Paul and Barnabas part; Paul chooses Silas.

label: Derbe
verse_text: He came to Derbe and Lystra; and behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timothy, the son of a Jewess who believed, but his father was a Greek.
note: Acts says only “through Syria and Cilicia” (15:41). Our line takes the Roman road through Tarsus, Paul’s home city, and over the Taurus.

label: Lystra
verse_text: He came to Derbe and Lystra; and behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timothy, the son of a Jewess who believed, but his father was a Greek.
note: Timothy joins them.
letter_text: Because of this I have sent Timothy to you, who is my beloved and faithful child in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways which are in Christ, even as I teach everywhere in every assembly.
letter_why: Paul calls Timothy “my beloved and faithful child in the Lord”.

label: Iconium
verse_text: As they went on their way through the cities, they delivered the decrees to them to keep which had been ordained by the apostles and elders who were at Jerusalem.

label: Phrygia and Galatia
verse_text: When they had gone through the region of Phrygia and Galatia, they were forbidden by the Holy Spirit to speak the word in Asia.
note: Acts names regions here, not towns, and says the Spirit kept them from Asia. Our line passes Antioch in Pisidia.

label: Troas
verse_text: A vision appeared to Paul in the night. There was a man of Macedonia standing, begging him and saying, “Come over into Macedonia and help us.”
note: Kept out of Bithynia too, they come down to the coast. A night vision: “Come over into Macedonia and help us.”

label: Samothrace
verse_text: Setting sail therefore from Troas, we made a straight course to Samothrace, and the day following to Neapolis;

label: Neapolis
verse_text: Setting sail therefore from Troas, we made a straight course to Samothrace, and the day following to Neapolis;

label: Philippi
verse_text: A certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, one who worshiped God, heard us. The Lord opened her heart to listen to the things which were spoken by Paul.
note: Lydia believes. Paul and Silas are beaten and jailed, and sing at midnight.
letter_text: but having suffered before and been shamefully treated, as you know, at Philippi, we grew bold in our God to tell you the Good News of God in much conflict.
letter_why: Paul recalls being “shamefully treated, as you know, at Philippi”.

label: Amphipolis
verse_text: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.

label: Apollonia
verse_text: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.

label: Thessalonica
verse_text: Paul, as was his custom, went in to them; and for three Sabbath days reasoned with them from the Scriptures,
note: Three Sabbaths in the synagogue, then a riot.
letter_text: For even in Thessalonica you sent once and again to my need.
letter_why: The Philippians sent help to him in Thessalonica, “once and again”.

label: Berea
verse_text: Now these were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, examining the Scriptures daily to see whether these things were so.
note: The Bereans examine the Scriptures daily.

label: Athens
verse_text: Paul stood in the middle of the Areopagus and said, “You men of Athens, I perceive that you are very religious in all things.
note: Paul speaks on the Areopagus. Acts says he was sent “to the sea” (17:14), so the map takes him to Athens by ship.
letter_text: Therefore when we couldn’t stand it any longer, we thought it good to be left behind at Athens alone,
letter_why: “We thought it good to be left behind at Athens alone.”

label: Corinth
verse_text: He lived there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
note: A year and six months. Gallio, proconsul of Achaia, hears the case against him.
letter_text: I was with you in weakness, in fear, and in much trembling.
letter_why: “I was with you in weakness, in fear, and in much trembling.”

label: Cenchreae
verse_text: Paul, having stayed after this many more days, took his leave of the brothers, and sailed from there for Syria, together with Priscilla and Aquila. He shaved his head in Cenchreae, for he had a vow.
note: Corinth’s eastern port. Paul cuts his hair for a vow.
letter_text: I commend to you Phoebe, our sister, who is a servant of the assembly that is at Cenchreae,
letter_why: Paul commends Phoebe, “a servant of the assembly that is at Cenchreae”.

label: Ephesus
verse_text: He came to Ephesus, and he left them there; but he himself entered into the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews.
note: A short stay; he promises to return “if God wills”.

label: Caesarea
verse_text: When he had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the assembly, and went down to Antioch.

label: Jerusalem
verse_text: When he had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the assembly, and went down to Antioch.
note: Acts says he “went up and greeted the assembly”. Most read this as Jerusalem.

label: Antioch
verse_text: When he had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the assembly, and went down to Antioch.
note: Acts does not say how he went down to Antioch. Our line takes the coast road.

label: Antioch
verse_text: Having spent some time there, he departed and went through the region of Galatia and Phrygia, in order, establishing all the disciples.
note: After “some time” in Antioch, he sets out again.

label: Galatia and Phrygia
verse_text: Having spent some time there, he departed and went through the region of Galatia and Phrygia, in order, establishing all the disciples.
note: Acts says he went “through the region of Galatia and Phrygia, in order, establishing all the disciples”. Our line visits the churches of the first journey.

label: Ephesus
verse_text: This continued for two years, so that all those who lived in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
note: Two years and three months: the synagogue, then the school of Tyrannus, then the riot in the theatre.
letter_text: But I will stay at Ephesus until Pentecost,
letter_why: “I will stay at Ephesus until Pentecost.”

label: Troas
verse_text: Now when I came to Troas for the Good News of Christ, and when a door was opened to me in the Lord,
note: Acts says only that he left for Macedonia (20:1). Paul’s own letter puts Troas on the way. How he got there is not said.

label: Macedonia
verse_text: After the uproar had ceased, Paul sent for the disciples, took leave of them, and departed to go into Macedonia.
note: Acts names the region. Our line lands at Neapolis and goes up to Philippi.
letter_text: For even when we had come into Macedonia, our flesh had no relief, but we were afflicted on every side. Fightings were outside. Fear was inside.
letter_why: “When we had come into Macedonia, our flesh had no relief.”

label: Greece
verse_text: When he had spent three months there, and a plot was made against him by Jews as he was about to set sail for Syria, he determined to return through Macedonia.
note: Three months in “Greece”. Most read this as Corinth, where Paul wrote Romans.
letter_text: Gaius, my host and host of the whole assembly, greets you. Erastus, the treasurer of the city, greets you, as does Quartus, the brother.
letter_why: Paul sends greetings from Gaius, his host, and Erastus, “the treasurer of the city”.

label: Philippi
verse_text: We sailed away from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread, and came to them at Troas in five days, where we stayed seven days.
note: A plot against him turns him back through Macedonia. He sails after the days of Unleavened Bread.

label: Troas
verse_text: We sailed away from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread, and came to them at Troas in five days, where we stayed seven days.
note: Seven days. Eutychus falls from a window during Paul’s long talk.

label: Assos
verse_text: But we, going ahead to the ship, set sail for Assos, intending to take Paul aboard there; for he had so arranged, intending himself to go by land.
note: Paul goes by land, on foot, while the others sail round.

label: Mitylene
verse_text: When he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and came to Mitylene.

label: Chios
verse_text: Sailing from there, we came the following day opposite Chios. The next day we touched at Samos and stayed at Trogyllium, and the day after we came to Miletus.

label: Samos
verse_text: Sailing from there, we came the following day opposite Chios. The next day we touched at Samos and stayed at Trogyllium, and the day after we came to Miletus.

label: Miletus
verse_text: From Miletus he sent to Ephesus and called to himself the elders of the assembly.
note: He calls the elders of Ephesus and says goodbye: “you all … will see my face no more.”

label: Cos
verse_text: When we had departed from them and had set sail, we came with a straight course to Cos, and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

label: Rhodes
verse_text: When we had departed from them and had set sail, we came with a straight course to Cos, and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

label: Patara
verse_text: Having found a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we went aboard and set sail.
note: They change to a ship crossing to Phoenicia.

label: Tyre
verse_text: Having found disciples, we stayed there seven days. These said to Paul through the Spirit that he should not go up to Jerusalem.
note: Seven days. They pass Cyprus on the left. The disciples tell Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.

label: Ptolemais
verse_text: When we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais. We greeted the brothers and stayed with them one day.

label: Caesarea
verse_text: Coming to us and taking Paul’s belt, he bound his own feet and hands, and said, “The Holy Spirit says: ‘So the Jews at Jerusalem will bind the man who owns this belt, and will deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.’”
note: At Philip’s house. Agabus binds his own hands and feet with Paul’s belt.

label: Jerusalem
verse_text: When we had come to Jerusalem, the brothers received us gladly.
note: The brothers receive them gladly. Days later Paul is seized in the temple.
letter_text: But now, I say, I am going to Jerusalem, serving the saints.
letter_why: “Now I say, I am going to Jerusalem, serving the saints.”

label: Caesarea
verse_text: When it was determined that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.
note: Two years a prisoner here. He appeals to Caesar and sails as a prisoner.

label: Sidon
verse_text: The next day, we touched at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly and gave him permission to go to his friends and refresh himself.

label: Myra
verse_text: When we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
note: They sail under the lee of Cyprus, against the wind, then change to a grain ship of Alexandria.

label: Cnidus
verse_text: When we had sailed slowly many days, and had come with difficulty opposite Cnidus, the wind not allowing us further, we sailed under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.
note: “Sailed slowly many days, and had come with difficulty.”

label: Salmone
verse_text: When we had sailed slowly many days, and had come with difficulty opposite Cnidus, the wind not allowing us further, we sailed under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.

label: Fair Havens
verse_text: With difficulty sailing along it we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.
note: Paul warns them not to sail on. “The Fast had now already gone by”: autumn.

label: Cauda
verse_text: Running under the lee of a small island called Clauda, we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat.
note: The storm wind Euraquilo seizes the ship.

label: Malta
verse_text: When we had escaped, then they learned that the island was called Malta.
note: Shipwrecked; all 276 reach land. Three months on the island.

label: Syracuse
verse_text: Touching at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.
note: Three days in port.

label: Rhegium
verse_text: From there we circled around and arrived at Rhegium. After one day, a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli,

label: Puteoli
verse_text: From there we circled around and arrived at Rhegium. After one day, a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli,
note: Brothers ask them to stay seven days.

label: Forum of Appius
verse_text: From there the brothers, when they heard of us, came to meet us as far as The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.
note: Believers from Rome walk out to meet him on the Appian Way.

label: Three Taverns
verse_text: From there the brothers, when they heard of us, came to meet us as far as The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.
note: “When Paul saw them, he thanked God, and took courage.”

label: Rome
verse_text: When we entered into Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard, but Paul was allowed to stay by himself with the soldier who guarded him.
note: Two whole years in his own rented house, preaching “with all boldness, without hindrance”.
letter_text: So as much as is in me, I am eager to preach the Good News to you also who are in Rome.
letter_why: Written years before: “I am eager to preach the Good News to you also who are in Rome.”
